Alaska.Ai — Anchorage Desk Draft

2026-09-04 · branch claude/linkedin-desk-2026-09-04

Copy this for LinkedIn

Curtis Thayer, CEO of the Alaska Energy Authority, told the Anchorage Daily News that a federal filing claiming a tie-in to AEA’s $400 million Cook Inlet PowerLink was “dead wrong.” AEA, he says, was never contacted.

Thayer is CEO and Executive Director of AEA, the Anchorage-headquartered agency that finances and operates Railbelt grid infrastructure, including the PowerLink submarine transmission project serving the Anchorage-area load center.

The trigger was a preliminary permit application at FERC. DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC proposed a 100-megawatt underwater AI data center off Nikiski, roughly 350 tidal turbines and 66 subsea server “hives,” described in the filing as designed to tie into AEA’s Cook Inlet PowerLink. Per the Anchorage Daily News on August 19, Thayer said AEA had never been contacted by the company. “It’s extremely disappointing that they would send something to FERC without contacting us,” he said.

The binary he owned was narrow. Let a claimed partnership with a $400 million public asset sit unchallenged in the federal record, or say on the record that it doesn’t exist.

He chose refutation, and it was the right call. A federal permitting record is a durable document, and an unverified interconnection claim inside it does real work for a developer. It signals to reviewers and to capital that a $400 million state-backed line is already in the plan.

Correcting that early costs AEA almost nothing, and it keeps a public asset from supplying free credibility to a developer AEA says it had never spoken with. It also tells the next speculative filer that Railbelt infrastructure isn’t a plug-and-play backdrop for an AI data center pitch.

The tension underneath is unresolved. Alaska’s utilities are courting exactly this class of load, and Chugach Electric has said it needs large new loads to spread fixed costs across a shrinking customer base. A 100-megawatt tidal-powered data center is, on paper, the kind of load that math wants. Thayer’s correction was justified, but it landed as a public no rather than an opening to talk. Whether AEA treats this as a one-off record correction or as its standing posture toward data center developers will say a lot about how Alaska competes for this investment.

The window is open now. FERC’s comment and intervention period on Project No. 15423-000 opened September 4, 2026. Watch whether AEA files formal comments or moves to intervene, whether DeepGreen amends or withdraws the PowerLink interconnection claim, and how Kenai Peninsula Borough stakeholders weigh in. Watch too whether this becomes the template for Railbelt responses to North Slope and Mat-Su proposals.

Was public refutation the whole answer here, or does AEA now owe developers a published front door for interconnection questions before the next filing lands?

#AlaskaAI #EnergyPolicy #GridPolicy #DataCenters

Editor note:
TARGET. Curtis Thayer, CEO and Executive Director, Alaska Energy Authority (Anchorage). Decision dated 19 Aug 2026, inside the 60-day window. No window broadening was needed. All eight gate points plus the conflict screen passed.

SOURCING CAVEAT (read this one). The validator set confidence to MEDIUM for a specific reason. Both news sources trace back to a single original ADN interview. The Center Square is a genuinely independent outlet with a separate reporter, but it attributes Thayer's quote to "told the Anchorage Daily News" rather than to its own reporting. The Federal Register / FERC notice (Project No. 15423-000) independently confirms that DeepGreen's filing exists and says what we say it says, but it does not corroborate Thayer's rebuttal. The post is written to respect that. The "never contacted" claim appears three times and is attributed to Thayer or AEA every single time, and the desk calls DeepGreen's assertion "unverified" rather than false.

EDIT LOOP. Cycle 1 came back REVISE on two honesty grounds. The hook and the structural read were stating "AEA had never been contacted" as bare fact. Both were fixed with inline attribution ("AEA, he says, was never contacted" and "a developer AEA says it had never spoken with"). Cycle 2 returned SHIP. One further precision edit was applied from the editor's optional list, restoring the dossier's exact wording on Chugach Electric ("large new loads" and "shrinking customer base").

ONE EDITOR REQUEST DECLINED. Cycle 1 also asked for a HEADLINE block inside out/draft_v1.md. That is a default-rules artifact and does not apply to this column. The Anchorage Desk writer returns the cover headline in a separate block that goes straight to the image renderer, and out/final_post.md is copied verbatim into LinkedIn, so a HEADLINE line inside it would ship as visible post text. The headline exists and is on the cover image.

SCORING. 8.22 / 10 weighted against config/desk_rubric.yaml, above the 8.0 threshold, with all nine hard-fail checks passing. No additional scoring cycles were needed. Weakest criterion was Readability at 7, where the scorer asked for two dense paragraphs to be split. That was applied after scoring, at sentence boundaries, with no wording changed, so every hard-fail check still holds. Final post is 449 words and 2,874 characters including the hashtag line, against the 350-475 word and 3,000 character caps.

IMAGE PATH. The routine prompt names the alaska-ai-brief template. The repo's own skill files now supersede that: alaska-ai-brief is marked "EMERGENCY FALLBACK ONLY" and alaska-ai-artwork is the primary path for every column. This run followed the repo skills and produced bespoke editorial art. Kicker, role slot, and byline are unchanged from the routine spec (ANCHORAGE DESK / OPERATOR / empty byline).

SLICE HEALTH. All four scout slices reported "thin." The validator dropped six of seven candidates: Jay Byam (Kartorium/RESPEC asset transfer) and the two UAA RAISE candidates on genuine single-sourcing, Nolan Klouda and Sean McLaughlin because their "decisions" were advocacy or a product rollout rather than a decision, and Dale Knipp on a February date far outside the window. Thayer was the only candidate holding the full spine.

DELIBERATELY PASSED OVER. The Anchorage Assembly approved the APD Real-Time Crime Center contract 8-4 on 1 Sep 2026. That is a real, in-window, primary-source municipal AI decision and would ordinarily be a strong target. It was skipped because the desk has run three consecutive issues on that exact thread (Sean Case, Keith McCormick, Sydney Scout). If you want it covered, a fourth angle is available and the vote count gives you a named-sponsor hook.

NO STALLS. All six subagents returned inside the timeout. No transient-error retries were needed.

IMAGE HOSTING SWAP. The base64-inline body came to 2,210,105 bytes, far over the 100 KB ceiling, so the email references the cover art at its permanent GitHub raw URL on this run's branch instead. The URL was verified with a HEAD request after the push and returns HTTP 200, content-type image/png, 1,647,215 bytes.

ART PIPELINE. Bespoke cover art, style family halftone_section (halftone screen crossed with blueprint annotation grammar), composition horizon_band, hue family red, seed 4192, paper plus five inks. Cleared every dedup cooldown against the last sixteen issues across all four columns. Four eval passes. Iteration 1 failed on concept, the dashed spur arced over the cable and read as a crossing rather than a gap, plus two blur smudges. Iteration 2 fixed the gap but the motto collided with the shoreline and labels ran dark on dark. Iteration 3 resolved the layout but the rotors read as a wind farm. Iteration 4 ships at a weighted 8.59 with no dimension below 7, and qa_check.py passes. Two script syntax crashes occurred in between and were fixed; those are crashes, not eval passes. Residual blemish, the depth-scale labels sit faint and the 0 M tick crowds the waterline.

Sources

  • Anchorage Daily News (PRIMARY SOURCE) — 2026-08-19 — Underwater data center proposed for Alaska's Cook Inlet by East Coast company — carries Thayer's refutation verbatim
  • The Center Square (CORROBORATOR, independent of subject) — 2026-08-24 — Independent outlet, separate reporter, covers the AEA/DeepGreen dispute with added context. Note: attributes Thayer's quote to ADN, so the two news sources share one original interview.
  • Federal Register / FERC, Project No. 15423-000 (CORROBORATOR, independent of subject) — 2026-09-04 — DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC notice of preliminary permit application accepted for filing; comment and intervention period opens. Corroborates the underlying filing, not the rebuttal.

Editor's report card

CriterionScoreWeightNotes
Hook strength80.1First paragraph (~216 chars) names Curtis Thayer, his role, and the concrete decision (refuting the FERC tie-in claim as 'dead wrong') before the fold. Decision is the hook, not the bio. Docked slightly because the block is dense rather than a clean two-line punch.
Subject + decision load-bearing for AK80.16Thayer's accountability is not soft; he owns the refutation outright. Consequence names sector (energy/AI infrastructure), dollar figure ($400M PowerLink), affected actors (DeepGreen, Kenai Peninsula stakeholders, future filers), and timeframe (Sept 4 comment window). Docked one tier because the decision is a reactive public correction rather than a capital, procurement, or funding allocation.
Subject identification fidelity90.1Full name, title ('CEO and Executive Director'), org (AEA), and explicit Anchorage tie all match desk_dossier.json exactly. No invented biographical detail.
Decision specificity + primary-source80.14What/when/binary all explicit and sharp, decision dated 2026-08-19, in-window under the 60-day override. Primary source (Anchorage Daily News) named inline. Corroboration present but implicit: the post uses Federal Register-sourced detail to corroborate the underlying filing but never surfaces that Thayer's rebuttal is single-sourced to ADN.
Structural read90.13Takes a genuine, earned position ('He chose refutation, and it was the right call') and then names the real, proportionate tension (Chugach's appetite for large loads vs. a public no). post_001 energy: analytical, structural, not hedged mush, not boosterism, not manufactured criticism.
Forward implication80.08Names a live, dated trigger (FERC comment/intervention window opened Sept 4, 2026) and concrete watch items. Specific rather than 'watch this space,' though presented as a list of possibilities rather than one crisp single trigger.
Voice match80.1Analytical, business-literate, plain-language explanation of a regulatory mechanism, matching post_001's register. No hagiographic verbs, no press-release recap, no banned phrases. One mildly breezy turn ('the kind of load that math wants') is minor drift, not disqualifying.
Readability (LinkedIn)70.05449 body words and ~2,860 total characters both comfortably inside the windows. Two paragraphs ran 5-8 sentences each, longer than the tight 2-4 sentence target. ORCHESTRATOR NOTE: after scoring, those two paragraphs were split at sentence boundaries with no wording changed, addressing this exact point.
Engagement question90.04Specific, debatable, tied directly to the decision's structural tension. No CTA, no rhetorical softener.
Credibility guard80.1Bio recap minimal; decision treatment dominates word count. Both quotes verbatim matches to desk_dossier.json with correct source_url. Attribution honest and appropriately hedged rather than overclaiming independent confirmation of the rebuttal. Held back from 9-10 only because the post never signals that corroboration for Thayer's account is thinner than for the filing's existence.

Weighted total: 8.22 / 10 · Threshold: 8.0 · Ship: yes
